[Condoman](https://www.google.com/search?q=condoman&kgmid=/g/11xlgtvj8k#-BBg) is a prominent Indigenous Australian superhero character created for a sexual health campaign, particularly aiming to encourage safe sex and the use of condoms. [1, 2] 
Key Aspects of the Condoman Campaign:

* Origin: Developed in North Queensland by Indigenous health workers as a culturally appropriate role model to promote safe sex.
* Appearance & Inspiration: Inspired by The Phantom comic character, Condoman was portrayed as a "respected, beautiful, gorgeous black man" wearing a distinct costume.
* Message: The campaign aimed to reduce STI and HIV transmission rates in communities, often using the slogan "Don't be shame, be game. Use condom" (originally "Use frenchies").
* Impact: The campaign gained national attention, featuring posters and media to encourage condom use among young people.
* Evolution: In 2009, a female counterpart named Lubelicious was introduced. [1, 2, 3] 

Contextual Information:

* Condom Purpose: [Condoms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Condom) are latex or non-latex sheaths used for contraception and preventing [STIs](https://fphandbook.org/chapter-14-male-condoms).
* Usage: It is advised to use water-based lubricants, check expiry dates, and ensure proper storage.
* History: The term "condom" has an unknown, possibly apocryphal origin, while modern condoms began around the 1840s. [4, 5, 6, 7, 8]
